architecture_principles: physical discovery comes before candidate ranking
the Agent uses measured rheological regularities as scientific tools rather than optimizing benchmark recovery
state-aware rheology, external chemistry evidence and process uncertainty serve distinct scientific roles
candidate selection should maximize usefulness and interpretability for the observed material failure mode
deterministic calculations are separated from language-model judgment
the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator are decision-quality controls, not components that need ablation to justify their existence
the final recommendation is frozen before physical adjudication
only concise auditable outputs are stored; hidden chain-of-thought is not scientific evidence
held-out result data are structurally removed before outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction payloads are assembled
external analogue percentages define supported regions, not exact local optima
performance mitigation and causal isolation are distinct experiment intents; single-factor attribution is not the universal default
among similarly supported candidates, the minimum sufficient intervention is preferred
architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V3.4.0 is an outcome-blind reconstruction of the preexperimental decision state using only evidence available before the validation result. It may support recovery of the scientific problem, intervention family, and formulation neighborhood, but it must not be described as a recovered contemporaneous machine record or as proof that the exact historical recipe was independently predicted.

core_scientific_tool.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
core_scientific_tool.role: Convert the paper's upstream findings into machine-usable design rules without exposing the validation formulation or its outcome.

evaluation_priority: physical wet-lab adjudication of the selected point
traceable use of measured local regularities
reproducibility of the recommendation under the same evidence contract
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_PREEXPERIMENTAL_RECONSTRUCTION_AGENT_V3
non_goals: proving that every internal Agent module is individually necessary through ablation
making architecture benchmarking the main scientific contribution
optimizing held-out-region recovery as the main objective
claiming that literature-prior proximity predicts the wet-lab outcome
replacing the material-science result with an LLM-systems paper
primary_agent_outputs: material regularities used in the decision
design implication derived from each regularity
measurement plan tied to the discovered failure mode
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that reconstructs the preexperimental decision state: it extracts material-response regularities from measured PUR rheology, selects an intervention strategy, and freezes one useful formulation-process experiment point without access to the later validation formulation or outcome.
required_scientific_sequence: state the positive material regularities and their boundaries
translate those regularities into a design objective
use external evidence to identify chemically plausible intervention directions
adjudicate robustness to reasonable alternative evidence interpretations
freeze one useful experiment point and a falsifiable measurement criterion
architecture.secondary_replay_role: Deprecated for the current study narrative. The active Stage-1 evaluation is a single outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction, not an Arm A/Arm B replay comparison.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode, upstream rheological regularities, evidence needs and measurement objective before candidate ranking
execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, formulation inspection and process-state audits
rank experiment points according to scientific usefulness for the discovered material problem
try to falsify the provisional recommendation and test scientific interpretability, leakage and claim boundaries
adjudicate whether the proposed point remains useful under alternative evidence priorities, process-state uncertainty and the skeptic's strongest objections
resolve proposer, skeptic and robustness records and make the final pre-result decision
programmatically validate and freeze the recommendation with timestamp, hashes, model, candidate state, uncertainty and falsifiable acceptance criterion

deterministic_decision_diagnostics.intervention_sufficiency_rule: Decision order is: failure mode -> experiment intent -> required intervention-axis coverage -> evidence-supported candidates -> minimum sufficient intervention. For performance_mitigation, candidates covering EVERY independently supported axis (acrylic_like, minor_tackifier_like) are compared first. Minimum sufficient intervention is a tie-break WITHIN that group only. A candidate that zeroes an independently supported axis is a partial-coverage / mechanistic control, not the default performance rank-1; it must not become rank-1 merely because zeroing that axis lowers modifier burden.
deterministic_decision_diagnostics.note: These are transparent decision diagnostics, not fitted property predictions. Exact literature-anchor distance is retained only for audit and is not a primary ranking objective. Performance-mitigation and causal-isolation scenarios are separated so that single-factor attribution is not the default for every experiment.

acceptance_criterion.claim: S1C41 is a conservative full-coverage acrylic-like plus minor-tackifier-like performance probe that can mitigate the local 120 C hot-hold drift failure relative to the high-drift E5 reference.
acceptance_criterion.criterion: Under a matched 120 C hold protocol with a pre-hold 120 C state anchor and either an S1C41 repeat or matched same-day E2/E5 reference, primary success requires SI_15_to_90 <= 0.465 and SI_15_to_60 <= 0.258. Strong success is SI values approaching the E1 low-drift regime, approximately within 2x E1 for both windows.
acceptance_criterion.failure_condition: Fail the mitigation claim if SI remains E5-like, if only static viscosity is measured, if state/run spread is comparable to the claimed effect without repeat or state-aware normalization, or if processability at 120 C becomes unusable for the design goal.
acceptance_criterion.measurement_window: 120 C thermal hold with measurements sufficient to compute SI from 15-60 min and 15-90 min; include 15, 60, and 90 min, with 30 min if feasible.

alternatives_considered.relative_reason: Also full-coverage and closer to the directly commensurate 19-20 wt% acrylic analogue region, but it uses a higher total modifier burden than S1C41; preferred only if the first test should strengthen the acrylic-axis challenge rather than use a conservative lower-bound full-coverage probe.

Full-coverage and best aligned with the repeated 19-20 wt% acrylic plus 5 wt% minor-resin analogue anchors, but larger total modifier burden and greater dilution of the E2 reactive core make it secondary under minimum-sufficient-intervention tie-breaking.

Full-coverage with lower total modifier burden, but the 2.5 wt% tackifier-like level is below the repeated 4.8-6.4 wt% minor-resin cluster, so it is better as a later robustness probe than the primary performance-mitigation experiment.
A useful acrylic-only mechanistic control, but it zeroes the independently supported minor-tackifier-like axis and therefore does not test the full performance-mitigation strategy.
Baseline/no-intervention control inside the measured local chemistry, but it does not test the resin-modification mitigation hypothesis for the established hot-hold drift failure.

judge_normalized.selection_rationale: Failure mode: the local material failure is 120 C hot-hold viscosity drift, established by E5 SI_15_to_60 = 0.515 and SI_15_to_90 = 0.931 versus much lower E1 drift; ordinary monotonic temperature thinning is not the failure. Experiment intent: the Planner requested performance_mitigation, so the first candidate should test the full independently supported mitigation strategy rather than a single-axis attribution control. Required intervention coverage: acrylic-like and minor-tackifier-like axes are independently supported, and S1C41 covers both with AC1920 15 wt% and TK100 5 wt%. Local experiments supplied the E1/E5 hold-drift contrast, E2 as the reactive-core anchor, the 80-130 C support including 120 C, and the high E2 repeatability/process-state risk. Paper-derived rheological rules supplied the state-aware vertical-shift regularity, the one-point 120 C state-anchor implication, and the warning that static viscosity/temperature response cannot substitute for hold stability. Curated PUR literature/database priors supplied the broad acrylic-modified region, directly commensurate acrylic anchors near 19-20 and 25 wt%, lower-region directional support near 15 wt%, and minor tackifier guidance around 5 wt% and below about 10 wt%. Conservative experimental-design constraints introduced here are full-axis coverage for performance mitigation, mandatory matched hold-window SI measurement, mandatory state anchoring/repeat or same-day reference, and minimum-sufficient total modifier burden only among sufficient full-coverage candidates. Skeptic objections are resolved by framing S1C41 as a conservative lower-bound full-coverage performance probe, not as a local optimum or exact literature match; by making state anchoring and repeat/reference controls mandatory rather than optional; and by requiring a composition/functionality audit before causal claims. Robustness objections are resolved by retaining S1C46 and S1C51 as predefined escalation candidates if S1C41 fails, rather than rejecting the dual-axis hypothesis from one lower-bound dose. Exact analogue distance is audit metadata only and is not the primary optimization objective.

action_requests.name: get_repeatability_risk
action_requests.reason: E2 is the reactive-core anchor for the candidate lattice, and its large measured run spread may make state/process realization dominate a single nominal viscosity value.

action_requests.reason: Understand the reactive-core anchor composition and its MDI/polyol/modifier fractions before comparing candidate chemistry axes or extrapolating from external analogues.

action_requests.reason: Confirm measured temperature support and choose an anchor temperature inside the 80-130 C local support, especially around the 120 C hold condition.

action_requests.reason: Retrieve source-level acrylic analogue anchors to distinguish directly commensurate coarse loading levels from noncommensurate evidence and avoid treating literature percentages as exact local optima.

action_requests.name: query_external_priors
action_requests.reason: Retrieve source-level tackifier range evidence, especially the conservative below-about-10 wt% guidance, before admitting any combined acrylic/tackifier intervention.

action_requests.reason: Retrieve directional stability evidence for modifier-containing PUR analogues, while keeping limitations explicit because chemistry, MDI, time scale, and process history differ from the local system.

candidate_evaluation_dimensions: Hot-hold stability at 120 C using SI over the local measured hold window, especially 15-60 min and 15-90 min
Nominal melt viscosity/processability at an anchor temperature within measured support, preferably including 120 C because it matches the hold condition
Temperature-response shape within 80-130 C rather than extrapolated temperatures
Repeatability and process-state sensitivity, including whether one-point state calibration is required
Acrylic-like modifier level relative to directly commensurate coarse anchors near 15, about 20, and 25 wt%
Tackifier-like modifier level relative to conservative minor-modifier guidance below about 10 wt%
Combined modifier fraction and dilution of the E2 reactive core
Stoichiometric plausibility and MDI/reactive-group balance, with unknown functionality and process history treated as uncertainty rather than imputed
Evidence type supporting each modifier axis: direct numeric analogue, directional stability evidence, or conservative extrapolation-control rule
Distance from measured original formulations and from external analogue domains
counterfactual_checks: Would a reactive-core-only E2-like candidate with no acrylic-like or tackifier-like modifier plausibly address the established hot-hold drift, or would it merely test baseline process state?
Would a single-axis acrylic-only intervention be preferable if the stated intent were causal isolation rather than performance mitigation?
Would a tackifier-only low-level intervention test a distinct hypothesis but provide less evidence-supported mitigation than a bounded acrylic-plus-minor-tackifier design?
Does the proposed region remain justified if the external 20 wt% acrylic examples are treated only as processability analogues rather than hold-stability evidence?
Does the proposed region remain justified if the 25 wt% acrylic comparative-stability evidence is treated as functionality-sensitive and noncommensurate with AC1920?
Would the same candidate still be selected if the objective penalizes SI more strongly than nominal viscosity, as required by the observed failure mode?
Does candidate selection avoid using any held-out validation formulation identity, outcome, or outcome-derived label?
planner.decision_goal: Select one evidence-bounded candidate formulation for a prospective hot-hold-stability mitigation experiment, after using the paper-derived state-aware rheology bridge and chemistry priors to define a defensible candidate region rather than an exact optimum.
design_implications: The next experiment should not optimize only a nominal viscosity at one temperature; it must measure hot-hold drift over the local hold schedule.

A performance-mitigation experiment may use a bounded multi-component intervention if acrylic-like and tackifier-like axes are independently supported and remain within conservative evidence-supported ranges.

State/process-history uncertainty must be kept explicit because E2 run spread is large; one-point or state-aware calibration should be considered if the canonical rheology summary confirms that state shifts dominate formulation-only prediction.

Candidate evaluation should prefer formulations that remain within measured temperature support, preserve processability near 120 C, and reduce SI during the 120 C hold relative to high-drift references.

External priors should be used as formulation-family and coarse-region support only: directly commensurate numeric anchors include acrylic levels of 15, about 20, and 25 wt% in PUR analogues; directional evidence includes tackifier/modifier effects on stability; conservative design principles include the 10 wt% tackifier upper bound and avoiding extrapolation beyond the grid.
material_regularities_to_use: Measured temperature sweeps for original formulations decrease monotonically from 80-130 C and are well described by Andrade-like descriptive fits, so temperature response is structured but should not be conflated with hot-hold stability.

E2 nominal temperature-sweep repeatability is poor, with CV roughly 0.46-0.58 and max/min ratios about 2.8-3.6 across 80-130 C, so a single nominal viscosity should not be treated as a unique material property without state/process calibration.
Thermal hold data directly separate stable and drifting behavior: E1 SI is about 0.095 from 15-60 min and 0.168 from 15-90 min, whereas E5 SI is about 0.515 from 15-60 min and 0.931 from 15-90 min.
The candidate grid is anchored on the E2 reactive core and varies acrylic-like modifier from 0-30 wt% and tackifier-like modifier from 0-10 wt%; candidate order and IDs do not encode rank.
External evidence supports acrylic-modified PUR regions around 15-25 wt% and minor tackifier regions below about 10 wt%, but these are analogue or directional anchors, not local optima.
External hot-hold-stability evidence supports modifier identity/functionality as a plausible stability variable, but it does not prove a molecular mechanism in the local system.
planner.physical_failure_mode: Hot-hold viscosity drift at 120 C is the established local failure mode: E5 shows large positive SI during the measured 15-90 min hold window, while E1 is much more stable over the same schedule. This is distinct from ordinary viscosity level and from monotonic temperature thinning.

Thermal hold at 120 C with the same or explicitly comparable time points used locally, including 15, 60, and 90 min if feasible
SI=(eta_t1-eta_t0)/eta_t0 calculated for 15-60 min and 15-90 min, not only an endpoint viscosity
At least one repeat or state-calibration measurement if the state-aware rheology summary confirms realization/process-state shifts dominate nominal formulation effects
Documentation of processing, hold prehistory, mixing, moisture exposure, and sampling sequence because these may alter apparent state
Composition audit for total acrylic-like, tackifier-like, combined modifier, polyol, and MDI fractions
uncertainty_triggers: If the state-aware summary shows that one-point state calibration is essential, candidate choice should require a calibration-compatible measurement plan rather than relying on nominal formulation-only prediction.

If the candidate requires acrylic-like loading above the largest directly commensurate anchor or tackifier-like loading above the below-about-10 wt% guidance, treat it as extrapolative and downgrade unless deliberately chosen as an uncertainty probe.
If hot-hold SI improves but nominal viscosity becomes outside a usable processability window, classify the result as only partially supported for the design goal.
If the new point shows large repeat/run spread comparable to E2, do not infer a chemistry effect without repeat or state-aware normalization.
If the temperature response is acceptable but hot-hold drift remains high, reject viscosity-level-only explanations of the failure mode.
If composition changes alter MDI/reactive-core stoichiometry in an uncontrolled way, separate stoichiometric uncertainty from modifier-family evidence.

provisional_acceptance_criterion.claim: A full-coverage acrylic-like plus minor-tackifier-like intervention mitigates the local 120 C hot-hold drift failure relative to the high-drift E5 reference.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.criterion: Primary success: SI_15_to_90 is reduced by at least 50% relative to E5, i.e. SI_15_to_90 <= 0.465, and SI_15_to_60 <= 0.258, under a matched 120 C hold protocol. Strong success: SI values approach the low-drift E1 regime, e.g. within about 2x E1 for both windows. Interpret only after checking state-anchor consistency and processability at 120 C.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.failure_condition: Fail the mitigation claim if SI remains E5-like, if drift is judged only from static viscosity without a matched hold-window measurement, or if run/state spread is comparable to the effect size without repeat or state-aware normalization.

provisional_measurement_plan.primary_response: Thermal-hold stability index SI=(eta_t1-eta_t0)/eta_t0 at 120 C, calculated for 15-60 min and 15-90 min; also record viscosity at each hold time and an in-range temperature sweep or at minimum 120 C static viscosity for processability/state anchoring.
provisional_measurement_plan.state_anchor_plan: Use a standardized mixing, reaction, moisture-exposure, sample-age, and loading history. Take a 120 C viscosity anchor before the hold-window analysis to locate the realization state; include at least one repeat or matched E2/E5 reference if resources allow because E2 showed large run spread.
provisional_measurement_plan.time_window: Matched local hold window with measurements at 15, 30, 60, and 90 min if feasible; primary adjudication on 15-60 and 15-90 min.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
